title: Cicatricial Alopecia Workup
subtitle: Decision tree: lymphocytic vs neutrophilic vs mixed

steps.prompt: Patient with hair loss. Permanent or active scarring noted on exam?

steps.detail: Take a 4mm punch from active disease edge. Submit for both vertical AND horizontal sectioning. Direct immunofluorescence if LE suspected.

branches.label: Crown centrifugal in patient of African descent
Boggy nodules + sinus tracts on vertex

steps.detail: Mixed lymphocytic + neutrophilic infiltrate at occipital scalp/posterior neck with keloidal papules. Treat with topical/intralesional steroids ± topical retinoids; refractory cases consider laser hair removal.
AGA, AA, telogen effluvium, anagen effluvium, traction, trichotillomania, syphilis, tinea capitis. See separate workup pathway.
Lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrate at infundibulum. First-line: high-potency topical + intralesional steroids; second-line: hydroxychloroquine, doxycycline, mycophenolate.
LPP variant with fronto-temporal recession + eyebrow loss in postmenopausal women. Add 5α-reductase inhibitor (finasteride/dutasteride) to LPP regimen.
Premature desquamation of inner root sheath. Most common cicatricial alopecia in Black women. Moderate-strength topical steroid + minoxidil + counsel on avoiding traction/heat/relaxers.
Photodistributed scarring with erythema, scale, dyspigmentation; DIF shows continuous granular IgG/C3 along DEJ. Hydroxychloroquine + sun protection + topical/intralesional steroid.

Tufted folliculitis (5-15 hairs from one ostium) at vertex. Long-course antibiotics (doxycycline + rifampin combo, or clindamycin/rifampin), topical/intralesional steroid, isotretinoin in refractory cases.

steps.prompt: Dissecting Cellulitis (Perifolliculitis Capitis Abscedens et Suffodiens)
steps.detail: Boggy nodules + interconnecting sinus tracts on vertex/occiput. Part of follicular occlusion tetrad. First-line: isotretinoin (long-course) + ablative therapy if refractory; biologics for severe disease.
